data.summary: status/brief undercount the queue: items held back ONLY by schedule.max_parallel_tasks are counted as neither ready nor blocked, so tasks.total != done+running+ready+blocked. REPRO (home-simulator repo, 2026-10-01, schedule.max_parallel_tasks=4): before any claim, ddflow status -> tasks {total:45, done:0, running:0, ready:4, blocked:22} (19 dep-free items vanish: C6, 36.5a, 37.1a-e, 37.6a, 38.9, 38.10...). After claiming 4 items: ddflow --json status -> {total:45, done:0, running:4, ready:0, blocked:22} (sum 26), while ddflow --json next lists 41 blocked, those 19 with reason='state', detail='parallelism cap reached (schedule.max_parallel_tasks=4)'. So next and status disagree on the same snapshot. Effect: operator reading status/brief ('Ready now: 4') concludes only 4 items are startable and cannot see the other dep-free ones; brief prints 'These 4 are independent' implying the rest are not. EXPECTED: one classification shared by next/status/brief/board: report cap-held items explicitly (e.g. tasks.held_by_cap or ready_capped, or count them as ready with a 'cap reached' note), and keep the invariant total == sum of buckets (add a test asserting it). Secondary: human 'ddflow next' output lists dependency-blocked items first and buries the cap reason; when the cap is the only reason, say 'N more items are ready but held by max_parallel_tasks=K' in the summary line.

claim/update --globs: repeated flag silently keeps only the LAST value, and a JSON-array string is split on commas into literal junk globs. Source: ddflow/surfaces/cli.py:390 cl.add_argument('--globs') (plain store; same for task add :314). REPRO (home-simulator 2026-10-01): 'ddflow --agent impl-34.10f claim 34.10f --globs a --globs docs/CHANGELOG.md --globs docs/RESEARCH.md --globs README.md ... --globs configs/default.toml' -> exit 0, lease.acquired event globs=['configs/default.toml'] only. The overlap check therefore never saw CHANGELOG/RESEARCH/README, and a sibling (34.8g) leased the same files; the conflict surfaced only later at 'update' and as a commit-hook warning. Second repro: impl-34.8g passed --globs '["home_simulator/world/speaker.py", "..."]' -> lease globs recorded as '["home_simulator/world/speaker.py"', '"home_simulator/config/speaker.py"', ... (brackets and quotes kept, nothing matches). EXPECTED: action='append' + comma split (or reject a repeated flag with exit 3), and validate each glob (reject [ ] " , warn when a glob matches no tracked file and no new path). Regression test: repeated --globs yields union; JSON-ish input rejected.

update --globs REPLACES the lease's globs instead of adding, with no warning, so an agent widening scope (the driver says 'ddflow update <ID> --globs ...' FIRST when you need to write outside globs) silently drops its earlier paths from conflict detection. REPRO (home-simulator 2026-10-01, item 34.10f): after claim, 'ddflow update 34.10f --globs "<5 paths>"' -> task.updated globs = exactly those 5; commit hook then listed only the 5. EXPECTED: either --add-globs/--globs+ semantics, or the driver/help text must say update replaces and show the before/after diff of globs on stdout. Also: 'ddflow show <id>' does not print the item's globs or the current lease globs, so the operator cannot see what a lease covers without reading the event log - add 'globs:' and 'lease: holder/worktree/globs' lines to show.

Lease records the WRONG worktree when a subagent claims via the parent's shared MCP connection with as_agent. REPRO (home-simulator 2026-10-01): parent session in .claude/worktrees/bridge-cse_01FvKyZJeWJTGdRnrN5jPjZE (MCP server cwd) spawned subagents with Claude Code Agent isolation=worktree; subagent impl-34.8g called ddflow_claim(as_agent=impl-34.8g) while working in .claude/worktrees/agent-a92981182770b640f. Its lease.renewed event recorded branch=worktree-bridge-cse_01FvKyZJeWJTGdRnrN5jPjZE worktree=.claude/worktrees/bridge-cse_01FvKyZJeWJTGdRnrN5jPjZE (the PARENT's tree), while siblings that claimed from the shell got their own tree correctly. Consequence: ddflow merge/review for 34.8g target the parent's (empty) branch, i.e. silently merge nothing or review the wrong diff, and two identities share one worktree. EXPECTED: the MCP claim must take an explicit worktree/cwd parameter (or refuse 'adopt' when as_agent differs from the connection identity and the worktree is already the connection's), and merge must refuse when the leased branch has no commits ahead of main while the item has an implement gate passed. Test: as_agent claim from a shared connection never adopts the connection's worktree.

ddflow review: same PARTIAL outcome exits with different codes by gate. REPRO (home-simulator 2026-10-01, item 34.10f, reviewer lan-deepseek-v4.1-flash): 'ddflow --agent impl-34.10f review 34.10f --gate rubber_duck' printed 'PARTIAL ... 5/6 chunk(s) reviewed' + 'recorded 34.10f.rubber_duck = partial' and exited 0; 'ddflow --agent impl-34.10f review 34.10f --gate critic --intent ...' printed 'PARTIAL ... 5/7 chunk(s)' + 'recorded ... = partial' and exited 3. EXPECTED: one exit code for partial regardless of gate (not 0, since 0 reads as a clean pass to scripts; 1 or a documented code). Related: in both runs chunk 4 hit the reviewer's 64k reasoning-token cap with no verdict; with default [[reviewer]].max_tokens/max_chunk_chars any diff > ~40k chars loses coverage. Suggest auto-split+retry of a truncated chunk at half size before reporting partial, and name the files in the unreviewed chunk in the output so the author knows what lacks coverage.

Follow-up to B5c32cbb5c1: a wrong worktree binding on an item is STICKY and blocks the correct merge. REPRO (home-simulator 2026-10-01, item 34.8g): after the MCP claim bound .claude/worktrees/bridge-cse_01FvKyZJeWJTGdRnrN5jPjZE, the owner ran from its real tree (.claude/worktrees/agent-a92981182770b640f): 'ddflow --agent impl-34.8g release 34.8g' then 'ddflow --agent impl-34.8g claim 34.8g --globs ...' -> 'the item's own tree, from an earlier claim ... cd .../bridge-cse... and work there'; with --no-worktree the bridge tree still shows in 'ddflow show 34.8g'. Then 'ddflow --agent impl-34.8g merge 34.8g --branch worktree-agent-a92981182770b640f --keep' refused: 'has its own worktree on worktree-bridge-cse_...; it lands that branch ... Drop --branch'. Without --branch it would merge the bound branch, which had ZERO commits ahead of main, and record the item merged. Operator workaround: fast-forwarded the bridge branch to the real branch, then merge -> d7fbf00. EXPECTED: (a) release/re-claim (or 'ddflow update <id> --worktree PATH') can rebind; (b) merge refuses (exit 3) when the bound branch has no commits ahead of base, instead of 'merging' nothing; (c) --branch allowed with an explicit --rebind. Also: 'complete' then printed 'standards/unit_tests passed on a different tree than the one you are completing' although the content was identical (0803640) - the tree fingerprint is taken from the bound (wrong) worktree, producing a false warning.

Commit hook resolves identity from the worktree, not from the lease holder/--agent, so it blames the owner for its own lease. REPRO (home-simulator 2026-10-01): impl-34.8g held the lease on 34.8g; 'git commit' in its own worktree .claude/worktrees/agent-a92981182770b640f printed 'paths ... leased by ANOTHER agent ... held by 34.8g (impl-34.8g) ... You hold: (no live lease)'. Every commit from a subagent worktree with an as_agent identity gets this false warning, which trains agents to ignore the real cross-agent warning. EXPECTED: hook honours DDFLOW_AGENT env / a per-worktree identity file written at claim time, and matches by lease holder; test: owner committing in its own tree gets no warning.

Global --agent flag only works BEFORE the subcommand. REPRO: 'ddflow brief --agent impl-34.8g --item 34.8g' -> 'unrecognized arguments: --agent' (exit 2); 'ddflow --agent impl-34.8g brief --item 34.8g' works. Agents naturally append flags, and the drivers/prompts tell subagents to 'pass --agent on every call' without saying where. EXPECTED: accept --agent (and other global options like --json, --repo) after the subcommand too (argparse parents= on each subparser), or document the position in every driver; test both positions.

LAN DeepSeek reviewer defaults make 'ddflow review' practically unusable: reasoning consumes the whole [[reviewer]].max_tokens (64k) budget before any verdict. REPRO (home-simulator 2026-10-01, reviewer lan-deepseek-v4.1-flash, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash): item 34.8g review of fe9e740: chunk 7/9 truncated in BOTH rubber_duck and critic; re-review of a 12K-char diff (72de30c): all 3 chunks truncated -> unavailable; each run took 27-44 minutes. Item 34.10f: chunk 4 truncated in both gates. EXPECTED: detect 'finish_reason=length with no content' and retry that chunk with a reasoning-effort cap (e.g. reasoning_effort/thinking budget param) or a smaller chunk, before declaring partial; ship a sane default max_tokens/max_chunk_chars for reasoning models; report the per-chunk file list for what went unreviewed; consider a wall-clock budget so a review cannot take 40 min silently.

Additional evidence for Bdc85898c40 (claim --globs): with TEN repeated --globs flags the claim recorded NO globs at all. REPRO (home-simulator 2026-10-01): 'ddflow --agent impl-34.8f claim 34.8f --globs a.py --globs b.py ... (10 flags)' -> 'claimed 34.8f', exit 0; 'ddflow --json show 34.8f' -> item globs [] AND lease globs []. (For 34.10f the same pattern kept only the last value, so the outcome differs by path - possibly the last value was a path the claim filtered.) Either way the agent ran with zero conflict coverage while believing it had declared 10 paths; a single comma-separated --globs on 'update' worked. EXPECTED: never accept a claim whose parsed globs differ from what was passed without saying so; print the recorded globs on every claim.

MCP ddflow_claim judges the MCP SERVER's cwd worktree, so the 2nd subagent sharing a connection is refused. REPRO (home-simulator 2026-10-01): parent session's MCP server cwd = .claude/worktrees/bridge-cse_01FvKyZJeWJTGdRnrN5jPjZE; subagent impl-34.8g's MCP claim had bound that tree (B5c32cbb5c1). Subagent impl-34.8f (own tree .claude/worktrees/agent-abfc3812795993a23) called ddflow_claim(as_agent='impl-34.8f', id='34.8f', globs=[...]) -> all-null result fields + 'this worktree is already bound to 34.8g, which is still open'. The same claim from the shell inside its own tree succeeded. EXPECTED: ddflow_claim takes a 'cwd'/'worktree' argument (Claude Code subagents can pass their own path), and the MCP instructions tell subagents to pass it; with as_agent set and no cwd, never adopt the connection's tree. Also: the all-null result object on refusal should be an explicit refusal with exit/status 3, not nulls.

ddflow review: chunk accounting is wrong and there is no way to re-review one chunk. REPRO (home-simulator 2026-10-01, item 34.8f, reviewer lan-deepseek-v4.1-flash): 'ddflow --agent impl-34.8f review 34.8f --gate rubber_duck' -> 'PARTIAL: 0 finding(s), 6/9 chunk(s) reviewed ... chunk 5/9: TRUNCATED' exit 3 - only ONE failing chunk named for THREE unreviewed; an earlier run said 8/9 with the same single reason. The same chunk (the core module) truncated deterministically in 3 runs of 25-40 min each; with no '--chunk N' / '--paths <files>' option the agent had to bypass ddflow with a direct model call to cover the file, and then recorded the gate passed from that out-of-band call (ddflow cannot verify it). EXPECTED: list every unreviewed chunk with cause + file list; add 'ddflow review <id> --gate G --chunk N' or '--paths' to re-run a subset and MERGE coverage into the gate outcome; on deterministic truncation, auto-split the chunk.

ddflow merge leaves the PRIMARY checkout mid-merge on a conflict (and doctor/recover don't notice), blocking every later merge by every agent. REPRO (home-simulator 2026-10-01): main had just landed 34.8f (5c2bcce, adds a CHANGELOG line); 'ddflow --agent impl-34.6e merge 34.6e' from the agent's worktree printed 'Auto-merging configs/default.toml / Auto-merging docs/CHANGELOG.md / CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in docs/CHANGELOG.md / Automatic merge failed; fix conflicts and then commit the result.' The primary (/ai/delian/src/home-simulator, on main) was left with MERGE_HEAD, 12 staged files and unmerged docs/CHANGELOG.md. Any later 'ddflow merge' fails with 'Merging is not possible because you have unmerged files'. 'ddflow doctor' -> 'Healthy'; 'ddflow recover --item 34.6e' -> 'Nothing to recover'. The agent is (correctly) forbidden from touching the primary, so the queue is wedged until an operator runs 'git merge --abort' there (done; then the same merge landed as 2166949 once the branch already contained main). EXPECTED: merge runs with a conflict check first (git merge-tree --write-tree, or merge --no-commit then abort on conflict), ALWAYS leaves the primary clean, exits 3 with 'merge main into your branch and retry'; doctor flags MERGE_HEAD/unmerged paths in the primary; test: conflicting branch -> exit 3 and primary has no MERGE_HEAD.
